previous_metadata.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: enhanced mobile-game screenshot concept for later image-to-video development.
Input image 1 is the ORIGINAL GAME SCREENSHOT and the edit target. Produce one finished, full-bleed portrait gameplay image with the same aspect ratio as the reference (390:694). No device, mockup frame, comparison panels, labels, watermarks or added slogans.
Preserve this exact game and visible state: same camera and composition, playfield shape, row/column structure, piece count and positions, recognizable character and item identities, functional colors, selection/tutorial cues, readable copy and counter values. Keep existing controls and HUD in their current regions and footprints. Do not add mechanics, objects, menus, rewards or moves. The viewer should immediately recognize the same playable game.
Retain its cheerful stylized casual-game character. Make the chosen improvement visible and professionally crafted while keeping symbols legible at phone size. Preserve the reference's gameplay geometry; no camera tilt, zoom, scene expansion or re-layout. Exact text must remain verbatim. The output is a visual concept, not a new gameplay state.
Apply only this experiment:
COMBINED PASS. Improve lighting, game graphics and existing UI together as one coherent premium casual-game treatment. Use soft motivated light, gentle contact depth and controlled highlights; refine existing characters/items with clean expressive forms and high-quality stylized materials; upgrade the existing UI with crisp exact typography, clean icons, balanced internal spacing and consistent polished surfaces. Preserve the original state, composition, counts, identities, functional colors and control footprints. Make the improvement clearly visible without making it a different game. No extra objects, heavy bloom, cinematic camera changes, noisy particles, invented controls or hidden symbols.

review.summary: Coherent warm materials, stronger contact depth and clear UI give the game a visibly finished treatment.
review.layout: The same overall network, open/closed rings, connectors, knot and tutorial cue remain in close correspondence; exact knot interweaving is not proven.
review.text: Source wording, including 'th rings', and all principal bottom copy/values remain readable.
review.identity: Copper open rings stay recognizable; closed rings are reinterpreted with conspicuous wood grain, changing their original mottled material identity.
review.scope_drift: Combined treatment is in scope overall, with material reinterpretation on closed rings and slight bottom-panel styling/footprint changes.
review.verdict: Promising combined visual target; verify ring material intent and topology before implementation.
